title: Tenant Pinset Controls and Automated Residency Attestation for Hosted API
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add tenant-level pinset controls that allow customers to declare preferred and forbidden regions, surface those controls in the Console, and generate attested evidence bundles for compliance audits. This work covers API + Console UX + backend evidence pipeline: tenant Pinset CRUD API, per-request routing metadata and headers, deterministic fallback policy options, a retention slider for audit bundles, and scheduled exports to customer-owned storage. Goal is to give customers clear, auditable assertions of where hosted API traffic was processed while preserving latency and availability SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant can create/edit a Pinset that specifies allowed_regions, preferred_regions, and exclusion_rules via API and Console UI
Routing honors tenant Pinset with three modes: strict (reject if not available), preferred (route to preferred regions, fallback allowed), and best-effort (no pin enforcement)
Each request routed for a pinned tenant emits an attestation record containing request_id, resolved_region, model_variant, routing_policy_sha, timestamp, and service-signature
Evidence bundles (daily/weekly/monthly) can be generated on-demand and exported to customer S3 or downloaded via Console, subject to tenant retention settings
Console shows Pinset history and audit log entries; retention slider controls how long evidence artifacts are stored in Redwood-managed storage
End-to-end tests covering strict-mode rejection paths, preferred-mode fallback, evidence generation, and export succeed in CI
decisions: Use a tenant-level 'pinset' object instead of per-route pins to reduce UI complexity and match most customer needs
Expose three routing modes (strict/preferred/best-effort) to balance compliance vs availability — strict will increment 'pin-strict-reject' metric
Evidence bundles will be signed by a rotating KMS key and include an immutable routing_policy_sha so audits can assert the exact policy used
Default retention for hosted evidence will be 90 days with tenant override up to 540 days; longer retention requires enterprise add-on
Fallback routing will prefer same-region dedicated capacity before crossing region boundaries to reduce egress and latency
technical_notes: API: tenant.pinset = {allowed_regions:list, preferred_regions:list, excluded_regions:list, routing_mode:string} exposed via Admin API and Console
Per-request header X-Redwood-Region-Resolution will be set by edge proxies with values: resolved_region, routing_mode, policy_sha, and will be recorded in audit logs
Attestation record format: newline-delimited JSON lines containing request_id, timestamp_iso, tenant_id, resolved_region, model, model_sha, policy_sha, server_node_id, service_signature
Evidence generation: daily manifest + gzipped NLJSON of attestations; archives signed and checksummed; manifests stored in internal bucket with lifecycle TTL matching tenant retention
Export: support S3 PUT integration with KMS-encrypted destination; support on-demand export via Console and scheduled monthly exports (cron-configurable)
Routing: runtime needs flag-aware routing to reject in strict mode or select fallback pools tagged with region affinities; requires update to router policy engine (runtime-1.20 change)
Observability: add metrics pinset.rule_evaluations, pinset.strict_rejections, attestation.generated, export.success/failure; surface recent failures on tenant Console page
Security: evidence bundles must be tamper-evident; use KMS-signed manifests and store signing-key rotation history for audits
blockers: Runtime routing engine API changes required (ENG-xxxx) — waiting on engineering RFC merge
S3 export flow needs IAM presigned URL capability from infra team
Acceptance tests depend on a test harness with deterministic multi-region routing; test infra slot allocated but not ready
